examples.text: Он будет делать наше новое шоу.
examples.trans: He will produce our new show.

examples.text: Настя, может, он сам доедет?
examples.trans: Nastya, maybe he can get there by himself?

examples.text: Я ему всё подробно объясню.
examples.trans: I will explain everything to him in detail.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, позвольте представить вам человека.
examples.trans: Hello, allow me to introduce a man to you.

examples.text: Нам очень приятно с вами познакомиться.
examples.trans: We are very pleased to meet you.

examples.text: Алло, да, я вас внимательно слушаю.
examples.trans: Hello, yes, I am listening to you closely.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.text: Извините, мне сейчас нужно ответить.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I need to answer this right now.

examples.text: Но этих китов сейчас очень мало.
examples.trans: But there are very few of these whales right now.

examples.text: Да, конечно, я сейчас тебе помогу.
examples.trans: Yes, of course, I will help you right now.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'free', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Он сказал, что вы сейчас свободны.
examples.trans: He said that you are available right now.

examples.text: Всё, свободен!
examples.trans: That's all, you can go!

examples.text: Это место свободно?
examples.trans: Is this seat free?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'any', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Любую боль можно ради любви потерпеть.
examples.trans: Any pain can be endured for the sake of love.

examples.text: В любой момент.
examples.trans: Any time.

examples.text: Любой человек это знает.
examples.trans: Anyone knows that.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'pain', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Любую боль можно ради любви потерпеть.
examples.trans: Any pain can be endured for the sake of love.

examples.text: У меня сильная головная боль.
examples.trans: I have a strong headache.

examples.text: Были дикие боли.
examples.trans: There were terrible pains.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'may'.

examples.text: Дмитрий Владимирович, а можно один вопрос?
examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, may I ask one question?

examples.text: А нам тоже участвовать можно?
examples.trans: Are we allowed to participate too?

examples.text: Можно всем, кроме нашего Вити.
examples.trans: Everyone is allowed, except our Vitya.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'love', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Любую боль можно ради любви потерпеть.
examples.trans: Any pain can be endured for the sake of love.

examples.text: Первый раз я запел про любовь!
examples.trans: For the first time I sang of love!

examples.text: Марина, послушайте, это всё из-за любви!
examples.trans: Marina, listen, it's all because of love!

потерпеть.gloss: to be patient for a while, to endure

meanings.en: to be patient for a while, to endure
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'терпеть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be patient for a while', forming an aspectual pair with 'терпеть'.
